samples.question: A row of ten square cells stands on a white card; each cell is filled either dark or pale.  A small solid arrowhead points up at exactly one cell, marking it.  Imagine that marked cell is removed from the row entirely and the remaining nine cells are slid together to close the gap, keeping their left-to-right order.  That shortened nine-cell row is not drawn anywhere; only after withdrawing the marked cell does it exist.  Is the shortened row a palindrome, reading the same left-to-right as right-to-left in dark and pale?  Answer with exactly one of: yes, no.
